quantifiers: For every finite-dimensional real vector space E, including dimension zero, every open subset U of E, and every f,g,h in U.
For every function Phi: U -> R differentiable at f,g,h. Differentiability here means a Frechet differential in the finite-dimensional real topology; write dPhi(y) in E*.

For the conditional cancellation statement, for every natural m including zero, every linear M: E -> R^m and every covector lambda in (R^m)* satisfying the two explicitly stated conditional hypotheses.
definitions: E* is the real algebraic dual (equivalently the continuous dual in finite dimension). The pairing <alpha,v> means evaluation alpha(v) for alpha in E*, v in E.
For x,y in {f,g,h}, D_Phi(x||y) := Phi(x)-Phi(y)-<dPhi(y),x-y>. No nonnegativity is implied by this notation.
M*: (R^m)* -> E* is the dual map, defined by (M*lambda)(v) := lambda(M(v)).
Exact moment matching means M(f-g)=0. The separate span condition means dPhi(h)-dPhi(g)=M*lambda.
semantics.metric: No metric is required. Any coordinate or Riesz implementation must explicitly identify the dual pairing and verify its translation; no indefinite norm is used.
semantics.units: Abstract finite mathematics: scalar Phi and dPhi evaluated on a displacement have the same units; no physical units or observation normalization are inferred.
exclusions: Convexity is not assumed or concluded.
Moment matching alone is not a sufficient premise for cancellation.
Cross-term zero may not be assumed.
No integration, Hessian bound, numerical likelihood, or entropy-budget certificate is in scope.
